correctness.rationale: Two independent sector decompositions establish the exact areas of the clipped polygon and its polar; multiplying yields the factorized product. An explicit derivative is negative on the full parameter interval using the elementary \(\beta\le\pi/4\) and \(\pi/4<\beta\le\pi/3\) split. Direct endpoint Taylor expansions and uniform Taylor bounds prove both sharp endpoint rates and the cubic high-sided limit. A standard-library independent computational check passed 417 assertions; no empirical statement is substituted for a universal proof.

value.rationale: The complete interpolation resolves the shape-dependent Mahler product on a canonical family joining the Euclidean disk to each regular polygon, a natural test path for planar volume-product extremal theory. The nonanalytic disk-side \((r-1)^{3/2}\) law, linear polygon-side law and universal cubic many-sided profile reveal quantitatively distinct regimes not supplied by endpoint inequalities or polygon-only formulas.
